content_html:
The carnivals in Cusco They are one of the most anticipated festivities of the year, a moment in which the imperial city and its communities are filled with color, music and tradition. Celebrated in February, these carnivals combine elements of andean culture with colonial influences, creating a unique experience that reflects the identity of the Cusco people.

If you are planning a trip to Peru, experiencing the carnival in Cusco is an unmissable opportunity to learn about local traditions up close. One of the main characteristics of the carnival is the «Carnival Game», where the population and tourists have fun throwing water, talcum powder and colored paints at each other. In the squares and streets, especially in the Plaza de Armas of Cusco, children, young people and adults participate in this tradition, creating an atmosphere of celebration and camaraderie.

Another tourist attraction of the carnival in Cusco is the music and dance. Folklore groups tour the city with colorful typical costumes, performing dances like the «Qashwa of San Sebastian», a traditional dance that celebrates fertility and the harvest. The comparsas fill the streets with life with Huaynos and Cusco carnivals, happy rhythms that invite everyone to join the celebration.

The Peruvian gastronomy It also plays a key role in this festival. During carnivals, families get together to share typical dishes such as pout or t'impu, a stew made of meat, potatoes, chickpeas and vegetables that symbolizes abundance. Furthermore, you enjoy the chicha de jora, a traditional drink that accompanies celebrations and is an essential part of the Andean gastronomic culture.

Another significant moment is the «Court of the Yunza», a tradition similar to "yunza" in the mountains and the "umsha" in the Peruvian jungle, where a tree decorated with gifts, streamers and balloons is installed. The participants dance around the tree and, with a machete, take turns cutting it until it falls. The couple who manages to knock it down is in charge of organizing next year's yunza, ensuring the continuity of the tradition.

The carnivals in Cusco are not only an expression of joy, but also a perfect opportunity for travelers to experience the most authentic side of the cultural tourism in Peru. Through these celebrations, the people of Cusco keep their ancestral customs alive, fusing the festive with the sacred in an unforgettable experience for both locals and visitors.

If you are looking for a destination that combines history, tradition and natureCusco is the ideal place. Take advantage of your visit to explore the Sacred Valley of the Incas, know the majestic Machu Picchu, tour the city and enjoy its exquisite cuisine. During carnivals, the magic of Cusco intensifies, offering a unique experience that will remain in your memory forever.

Come and experience the carnival in Cusco and discover why Peru It is one of the most fascinating tourist destinations in the world!
